$comment: Eight Washington local minimum wages, all above the country's highest state rate ($17.13). Two of them -- Renton and Everett -- step MID-YEAR on July 1 for their mid-size employer tier, which is the single most common way a Washington payroll run goes wrong. No Washington jurisdiction, state or local, permits a tip credit.

jurisdictions.name: Seattle
jurisdictions.coverage: All employers regardless of size. Seattle's employer-size tiers, and the old ability of small employers to count tips or medical-benefit payments toward minimum compensation, both ENDED on 2025-01-01.

sources.title: City of Seattle Office of Labor Standards -- Minimum Wage Ordinance
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session: '$21.30' effective January 1, 2026, and 'Starting January 1, 2025, all employers, regardless of schedule size, will be required to pay the same minimum wage.'

jurisdictions.name: SeaTac
jurisdictions.coverage: HOSPITALITY AND TRANSPORTATION employers only -- SeaTac's ordinance is sector-limited, unlike every other Washington local rate. Other SeaTac employers owe the state rate ($17.13).

jurisdictions.name: Tukwila
jurisdictions.coverage: Employers with 15 or more employees worldwide and a Tukwila presence, employers with $2 million or more in Tukwila revenue, or qualifying franchisees.

jurisdictions.name: Burien
jurisdictions.note: Updated 2026-10-23 to the City of Burien's own published 2026 rates (BMC 5.16 with Administrative Rule 2026-01), which Washington L&I's table now matches. Before that, this entry carried $21.63 / $20.63 with employers of 20 or fewer treated as not covered. The city's phase-in: the medium rate steps up to the large rate and the small rate trails it by a shrinking reduction. The city calls these the 2026 rates, but Ordinance 892 only took effect on 2026-05-27 (it repealed BMC 5.15); whether they apply back to 2026-01-01 was not confirmed, so effectiveFrom keeps the January 1 adjustment date. The ordinance is still the subject of a King County Superior Court request for guidance.

jurisdictions.name: Bellingham
jurisdictions.note: Bellingham's ordinance is defined as the Washington state minimum wage PLUS $2.00, so it moves automatically with the state rate ($17.13 + $2.00 = $19.13).

jurisdictions.name: King County (unincorporated areas only)
jurisdictions.coverage: Employers with 500 or more employees, for work performed in UNINCORPORATED King County only. Seattle, Tukwila, Burien, Renton and SeaTac are incorporated cities with their own ordinances above.

variants.label: Employers with 15 or fewer employees and $2 million or more in annual gross revenue
Employers with 15 or fewer employees and under $2 million in annual gross revenue

jurisdictions.note: 2027: the county's page states one exception: employers with 15 or fewer employees and annual gross revenue under $2 million may pay $2.00 less ($19.57); the other reduced tiers have ended, so midsize and small high-revenue employers pay the full $21.57. The three reduced tiers are a temporary phase-in that ends in 2031, when every employer pays the single county rate.

sources.title: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries -- Local Minimum Wage Rates
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. L&I's own consolidated table is the primary source for every Washington local rate and tier in this file -- and it corrected a figure that a secondary search had returned wrong (Renton's Level 2 mid-year step). Its Burien row read $21.63 / $20.63 on 2026-09-08; the source watch's 2026-10-22 snapshot shows it changed to $21.78 / $20.78 / $19.28, and the City of Burien's own page confirms those figures (see the next source).

sources.title: City of Burien -- Minimum Wage (BMC Chapter 5.16, Administrative Rule 2026-01)
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly (page dated October 13, 2026). Lists 2026 hourly rates of $21.78 for large employers (501 or more employees), $20.78 for medium (16-500) and $19.28 for small (15 or fewer), and 2027 rates of $22.49 large and $20.49 small. Its 2027 medium rate is stated as equal to the large rate, which conflicts with the same page's note that medium employers' reduction shrinks by $1 a year; 2027 is therefore not entered here. The companion news post (https://www.burienwa.gov/news_events/city_newsroom/news_announcements/updates_on_buriens_minimum_wage) records Ordinance 892 (approved 2026-05-18, effective 2026-05-27) and that the request for court guidance on BMC 5.16 was unresolved as of May 2026.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Labor Center -- Inventory of US City and County Minimum Wage Ordinances
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. The standing national census of local minimum wage ordinances -- used here to establish WHICH jurisdictions exist (so none is silently omitted), with each rate then cross-checked against a second source.

knownGaps: Tacoma repealed its local ordinance in December 2019 once the state rate overtook it; it is deliberately absent rather than carried at $0.

Burien's ordinance remains subject to litigation arising from competing 2025 ballot measures. The city's own published figures (matched by L&I) are used; a court ruling could change them mid-year. Whether the 2026 rates apply back to January 1 or from Ordinance 892's 2026-05-27 effective date was not confirmed, and the city's 2027 medium-employer rate is internally inconsistent on its page, so no 2027 Burien entry exists.
SeaTac's ordinance covers only hospitality and transportation employers; the precise industry test is in the ordinance and is not modelled here.

provisional.note: Carried forward from the 2026 file on 2026-10-25 so that a 2027-dated query resolves instead of failing. Every figure is 2026's unless listed in updatedFor2027 (each with the state agency's own announcement or the statute). Remove this block only after every figure has been re-read against a 2027 source. LOCAL ORDINANCES ARE NOT YET UPDATED for 2027: many step on 1 January 2027 (e.g. Denver $19.84, Minneapolis $17.02, Seattle, Flagstaff, Albuquerque, Portland ME). The figures here are 2026's until each ordinance is re-read. 2026-11-06: Seattle, Burien and unincorporated King County were re-read from the cities' and county's own pages and updated; Tukwila, Renton and Everett pages answer 403 to automated requests and Bellingham's page still shows the prior-year dollar, so those stay at 2026 figures.

All employers regardless of schedule size.

City of Burien, Minimum Wage https://www.burienwa.gov/city_hall/laws_regulations/minimum_wage read directly 2026-11-06: 2027 large employer rate $22.49 ($21.7752 + 0.7185 CPI-W increase), medium employer rate equal to the then-current large employer rate, small employer rate $20.49 (BMC 5.16).

King County, Minimum wage in unincorporated King County https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/local-services/governance-leadership/local-government-for-unincorporated-king-county/minimum-wage read directly 2026-11-06: 'Starting January 1, 2027, the minimum wage for work done in unincorporated King County will be $21.57 per hour.
